newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Rights groups say hunger strike in PLO prisons.
newsitem.headline: Rights groups say hunger strike in PLO prisons.

text.p: Scores of Palestinian political prisoners held by the Palestinian Authority in the West Bank and Gaza are on hunger strike demanding their release, human rights groups and relatives said on Thursday.
They said some members of the Hamas Islamic Resistance Movement and the Marxist Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine (PFLP) have been fasting for 14 days.
A Palestinian official denied any of the PFLP or Hamas prisoners was currently fasting.
"Their complaints have been dealt with and no prisoners are now on a hunger strike," said the offical who declined to be named. He did not elaborate.
Palestinian human rights groups estimate at least 200 suspected activists of Palestinian factions opposed to Israeli-PLO peace moves are being held in West Bank and Gaza jails.

The Palestinian Authority last year rounded up hundreds of Hamas activists after a spate of suicide bombings inside Israel, but most have since been released. Dozens of PFLP activists were detained earlier this year following another guerrilla attack.
Many of the prisoners are being held without charges.
A Hamas leader in Lebanon said on Wednesday political prisoners in all Palestinian jails would begin an open-ended hunger strike on Thursday.
